problem_text:
A regional sales manager must conduct a one-day visit to 11 branch offices, each situated at distinct geographic coordinates within the territory. The offices are labeled as follows:

Office Alpha: Coordinates (11,78)
Office Beta: Coordinates (141,18)
Office Gamma: Coordinates (2,117)
Office Delta: Coordinates (126,185)
Office Epsilon: Coordinates (112,12)
Office Zeta: Coordinates (105,126)
Office Eta: Coordinates (117,112)

Office Iota: Coordinates (20,61)
Office Kappa: Coordinates (25,195)
Office Lambda: Coordinates (39,105)

Due to a road closure, direct travel between Office Alpha and Office Beta is impossible. Furthermore, due to scheduling constraints at a shared corporate facility, exactly one of two specific connecting routes must be incorporated into the itinerary: either the route between Office Beta and Office Gamma, or the route between Office Gamma and Office Delta.

The objective is to determine the shortest possible circular tour that visits each branch office precisely once before returning to the starting office, thereby minimizing total travel distance for the day.
